senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to engage in doing what is good
a person in the genealogy of Jesus

senses.subdomain: To Choose, To Select, To Prefer
senses.def: to make a choice of one or more possible alternatives
senses.comment: In a number of languages the choice of terms or expressions for ‘choosing’ or ‘selecting’ often depends upon either (1) what is chosen or selected or (2) the purpose for such a choice, for example, personal pleasure, rational evaluation, or outright prejudice.

senses.subdomain: To Choose, To Select, To Prefer
senses.def: to choose or select for the purpose of showing special favor to or concern for
pertaining to not being willing to do something
glosses: not of one’s own free will
not a matter of free choice
senses.comment: Expressions of ‘not being willing to do something’ may often be rendered as ‘being forced to do something’ or ‘doing something because one has to.’

senses.subdomain: To Think About, with the Implied Purpose of Responding Appropriately
senses.def: to not think about, and thus not respond appropriately to
to invoke divine harm if what is said is not true or if one does not carry out what has been promised
senses.comment: In Mark 14:71 ἀναθεματίζω is in many regards similar in meaning to ὄμνυμι (33.463), but ἀναθεματίζω specifically denotes a curse which was invoked by Peter if what he was saying was not true.

senses.def: to cause something to be completely overturned
(a figurative extension of meaning of ἀνατρέπω[a] ‘to overturn,’ 16.18) to cause serious difficulty or trouble with regard to someone’s belief
to build something up again after it has fallen

senses.domain: Stances and Events Related to Stances
senses.def: to straighten up from a bent over position
(an idiom, literally: straighten paralyzed knees) to gain encouragement by a strong resolve
senses.comment: See discussion at 23.170.

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: (derivative of ἀλλότριος[b] ‘stranger, foreigner,’ 11.74) to be a stranger or foreigner
to come to believe something to be true and to respond accordingly, with some emphasis upon the source
to shake something out or off, in order to get rid of an object or a substance
senses.comment: In a number of languages quite different terms for shaking will be required for the contexts of Acts 28:5 and Luke 9:5, since in the first instance it is an animate being which clings, and in the second instance it is simply a substance that adheres.|In a number of languages, however, the symbolic meaning of ‘shaking dust off one’s feet’ is not at all clear, so that it may be necessary to add a type of classifier to indicate that such an action symbolizes the breaking off of association. It is for this reason that the expression ἐκτιναξάμενος τὰ ἱμάτια in Acts 18:6 is often translated as ‘he protested by shaking the dust from his clothes.’

senses.def: (derivative of ἀρήν ‘lamb,’ 4.24) young of sheep (πρόβατον); often used for ritual sacrifice; or a sheep of any age
senses.comment: In the one context in the NT, namely, Revelation 13:11, in which ἀρνίον refers literally to a sheep, it is used in a phrase referring to the horns of an ἀρνίον. In such a context the reference is undoubtedly to a ‘ram,’ that is to say, the adult male of sheep.

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of ἀρνίον[a] ‘lamb,’ 4.25) a follower of Christ, with the implication of helplessness and dependence
glosses: a person who is like a lamb
senses.comment: Compare 11.30 and 11.31.

senses.def: a title for Christ
senses.comment: ἀρνίον[c] as a title of Jesus Christ occurs only in the book of Revelation, but it is used there more than twenty times. In contrast with ἀρνίον[b] in βόσκε τὰ ἀρνία μου ‘feed my lambs’ (John 21:15; see 11.29), designating people who need care and help, the supplementary components of meaning in ἀρνίον[c] involve the atoning sacrifice of Jesus Christ on the cross. Some persons have wanted to eliminate the notion of ‘lamb’ in this title, especially in the case of languages in which sheep are looked down on as relatively worthless scavengers (as is the case in certain tropical areas of the world), but in view of the significance of the symbolism of ‘lamb’ in terms of OT sacrificial practices, it is wrong to avoid a term meaning ‘lamb.’ A marginal note, however, may be necessary to explain the significance of this title.

senses.def: pertaining to being unwilling to be reconciled to others
glosses: unwilling to be at peace with others

senses.def: to express an unusually high degree of confidence in someone or something being exceptionally noteworthy
senses.comment: Whether in any particular context the boasting is legitimate or not depends upon what is boasted about. In a number of languages, however, quite different terms are employed, depending upon the differing degrees of justification for such boasting.

senses.def: to dip an object in a liquid

senses.subdomain: Processes Involving the Mouth, Other Than Eating and Drinking
senses.def: the grinding or the gnashing of the teeth, whether involuntary as in the case of certain illnesses, or as an expression of an emotion such as anger or of pain and suffering
senses.comment: In translating ‘they ground their teeth at him’ (Acts 7:54) it may be necessary to indicate the type of emotion which is involved in such an action, for example, ‘in anger they ground their teeth at him’ or ‘they showed their anger by grinding their teeth.’ It is essential to avoid an expression such as ‘to grit the teeth,’ which in English is a symbol of determination, not of anger.

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to grind one’s teeth) to express and manifest intense anger
senses.comment: As noted in 23.41, it is possible to understand the expression βρύχω τοὺς ὀδόντας in both a literal as well as a figurative sense. The persons may very well have ‘ground their teeth’ as a sign of their anger and fury, so that a statement about what such persons did could be true in a literal as well as in a figurative sense.

senses.def: to consume solid food
(a figurative extension of meaning of γεύομαι[a] ‘to taste,’ 24.72) to experience, probably focusing on personal involvement
an Athenian woman converted by Paul
to speak in a somewhat formal setting and probably implying a more formal use of language
to travel around through an area, with the implication of both extensive and thorough movement throughout an area
senses.comment: In order to express the meaning of διοδεύω, διαπορεύομαι[a], and διέρχομαι[b] in these types of contexts, it may be necessary in some languages to say ‘he went from one town to another’ or, as in Acts 13:6, ‘he travelled to all the places on the island’ or ‘… to the various towns on the island.’

senses.def: to go completely through an area

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to being in accordance with what God requires
pertaining to being in a right relationship with someone
glosses: being in a right relation with
one who has been put right with

senses.def: pertaining to being proper or right in the sense of being fully justified
to cause someone to become a slave
glosses: to make a slave of someone
senses.comment: In Acts 7:6 αὐτὸ refers to the preceding τὸ σπέρμα αὐτοῦ ‘his descendants.’

senses.def: to gain control over someone and thus make such an individual subservient to one’s own interests
glosses: to cause someone to be subservient to
to cause to be like a slave

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of δουλόω[a] ‘to enslave,’ 87.82) to be firmly bound by an obligation or a relationship
(a technical, legal term) a formal indictment or accusation brought against someone
each one of a totality in a distributive sense
to run or rush out quickly
a person in the genealogy of Jesus
to begin in a particular state or relationship
a state of embarrassment resulting from what one has done or failed to do
extension from a source which is outside
a position not contained within a particular area
the outside surface of an object
senses.comment: The manner in which ἔξωθεν[c], ἐκτός[b], and ὄπισθεν[c] may be rendered in particular contexts depends very largely upon what is being spoken about. For example, ἔξωθεν in 1 Peter 3:3 refers to the outward aids employed in making oneself beautiful, but instead of speaking of such objects as being on the surface or on the outside, it may be necessary to speak of those things which one puts on the body or what one wears.

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of ἔξωθεν[a] ‘from outside,’ 83.20) a person who is not a member of a particular in-group
senses.comment: In a number of languages it may be appropriate to render 1 Timothy 3:7 as ‘he should be a man who is respected by those who are not believers’ or ‘… by those who are not followers of Christ.’

senses.def: to marry the childless widow of one’s brother (the so-called levirate marriage; see
to be or to become ready for some purpose
to announce in a sudden and emphatic manner (with an implication of ‘blurting out’)
pertaining to being encouraged
to leap or jump onto a place or object
a major OT prophet
pertaining to being taught by God
senses.comment: In a number of languages the passive expression θεοδίδακτοί ἐστε in 1 Thessalonians 4:9 must be rendered in an active form, for example, ‘for God himself has taught you how you should love one another.’

senses.def: a long, oblong shield; used to protect the entire body in battle; made of wood, metal, leather stretched over wood, or plaited strips of wood or reeds
senses.comment: In some languages ‘shield’ is described as ‘protection one carries when one fights’ or ‘protection carried to prevent blows from the enemy.’ The phrase ἀναλαβόντες τὸν θυρεὸν τῆς πίστεως may thus be rendered as ‘take hold of faith as a protection against the enemy’ or ‘regard your faith as a protection to prevent the attacks of the enemy.’

senses.def: interrogative expressions of reason
= καί + ἐγώ; a reference to the speaker, with an added feature of emphasis in the form ἐγώ
senses.comment: The terminology ‘first, second, and third persons’ reflects the normal order in Greek in which the so-called first person always occurred first in any listing of participants. The second person would be in the second position, and similarly, the third person would be in a third relative position. To preserve that order in English, however, could imply impoliteness, and it is for that reason that it is preferable to translate John 10:30 as ‘the Father and I are one.’

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to do that which has a positive moral quality and which would normally produce a favorable response

senses.subdomain: Events Involving Liquids and Dry Masses
senses.def: a large flood with destructive force (more intense and extensive than πλήμμυρα ‘flood,’ 14.33)
senses.comment: In the NT κατακλύζω and κατακλυσμός occur only in 2 Peter and are used exclusively of the catastrophic flood in the time of Noah. Such a flood may be spoken of as ‘a flood that destroys’ or ‘much water which destroys.’

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of καταστρώννυμι ‘to spread out,’ not occurring in the NT) to cause the death of a number of persons, with the implication of bodies spread out over an area
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand this expression in 1 Corinthians 10:5 as meaning that the individuals died and that their bodies were strewn over the desert.

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: a state of pride which is without basis or justification
to receive something of considerable value which has not been earned
to receive a possession or benefit as a gift from someone who has died, generally a parent
glosses: to receive from a deceased parent
senses.comment: In some languages the process of inheritance must be made rather explicit, so that ‘he will inherit the property’ must be expressed as ‘he will become owner of the property which his father said he should have.’

senses.def: a room in the Temple used as a treasury
one who commands a ship
senses.comment: In some languages a captain is simply ‘the chief of a ship’ or ‘one who commands the sailors.’

senses.def: to speak or talk, with apparent focus upon the content of what is said
to speak of a person or object by means of a proper name
to use an attribution in speaking of a person
senses.comment: It is not always possible to determine from the context whether the act involved is an initial naming of a person or simply calling a person by a particular name. Likewise in the case of attributions or titles, it is not always possible to determine whether it is a matter of giving an attribution or title to a person or simply a matter of speaking of or to a person by means of such an attribution or title. In some instances the giving of a title may be made indirect. For example, in Matthew 1:23 the statement ‘and they will call his name Emmanuel’ suggests the giving of a title, but the process is stated in terms of how people will speak of this person.

senses.def: to mark the correspondence in the meaning of foreign expressions
senses.comment: The meaning of λέγω[d] must often be expressed in rather specific ways, for example, ‘which says in our language’ or ‘what is the same as what we say in our language.’

senses.def: to say something in order to explain more fully the implications or intent of what has been said

senses.subdomain: Have an Opinion, Hold a View
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to speak to oneself) to think about something without communicating the content to others
glosses: to say to oneself (often used to introduce a direct quotation of one’s thoughts)

senses.def: to wash the body
the mother of one’s own mother or father (with a possible connotation of affection)
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is necessary to distinguish between the grandmother on one’s father’s side and the grandmother on one’s mother’s side. There is no positive indication in 2 Timothy 1:5 as to the particular relationship involved, but one may assume that the grandmother Lois was the mother of Eunice, and therefore it would be the grandmother on the mother’s side.

senses.subdomain: Instruments Used in Marking and Writing
senses.def: a sheet of specially prepared animal skin on which one could write with pen and ink; books or scrolls made of such skin
senses.comment: In 2 Timothy 4:13 the reference may be to documents written on parchment or to blank sheets of parchment. Sheets of parchment were either sewn together in long scrolls or, in later developments, bound together into book form (see 6.66).

senses.subdomain: Instruments Used in Marking and Writing
senses.comment: As noted in 6.59, μεμβράνα[a]) or of books written on parchment (μεμβράνα[b]).

senses.def: marker of negative propositions

senses.subdomain: Markers for a Negative Response to Questions
senses.def: a marker of a negative response to a question
marker of negative purpose, often with the implication of apprehension

senses.subdomain: Not Able To Be Known, Secret
senses.def: (an idiom, probably an adage or traditional saying, literally: do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing) an admonition to do something without letting people know about it
glosses: to do something without letting the public know
senses.comment: It is rare that one can preserve this idiom, since in its literal form it may seem absurd. For many English-speaking people the meaning has already been twisted by common usage to mean ‘be sure to not let anyone know if you are performing something that is shady or illegal.’ Today’s English Version attempts to represent something of the impact of this idiom by translating “do it in such a way that even your closest friend will not know about it.”

senses.def: marker of negative purpose, often with the implication of apprehension

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: not above what is written) to act sensibly in not violating written rules and traditions
glosses: to act sensibly in keeping with rules

senses.def: a complaint which implies blame

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
senses.def: pertaining to having been in existence for only a short time
pertaining to that which is new or recent and hence superior to that which is old

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
senses.def: pertaining to a living being who is relatively young, often the younger of two objects
a relatively large room, often serving as a place for a wedding
senses.comment: Υἱοὶ τοῦ νυμφῶνος, literally ‘sons of the wedding hall,’ is an idiom denoting the bridegroom’s friends or the wedding guests (see 11.7).

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: a person who habitually drinks too much and thus becomes a drunkard
pertaining to having a thin cutting edge

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
senses.def: pertaining to a very short period of time, with the probable implication of special haste
senses.comment: It would also be possible to understand ὀξεῖς οἱ πόδες αὐτῶν ‘their feet are swift’ as being an idiom, but ὀξύς occurs frequently in non-biblical Greek with the meaning of ‘quick, swift, soon.’ In Romans 3:15 οἱ πόδες αὐτῶν is a metonymic expression meaning ‘the people,’ so that it is not simply the feet that are swift to shed blood, but it is the people who are quick to kill.

senses.def: a reference to a position in space (often used with ἐάν or ἄν ‘ever,’ 71.8, to mark an indefinite and unrestricted position in space)
a relative reference to a set of circumstances
to engage in intense struggle, involving physical or nonphysical force against strong opposition
senses.comment: In a number of languages a marked distinction is made between physical fighting and nonphysical contending with someone. It is therefore often impossible to carry over any terminology involving war or physical struggling to contexts in which one is speaking of interpersonal hostility or contention.

senses.def: (derivative of παραμυθέομαι ‘to comfort,’ 25.153) that which causes or constitutes the basis for consolation and encouragement
the presence of an object at a particular place
to come to be present at a particular place
to cause the process of burning to begin
senses.comment: As already noted in the series of terms listed in 14.63, languages differ appreciably in terms employed for different phases and results of burning. For example, to set something on fire for the sake of providing warmth may be expressed by quite a different term from that which is used in speaking of the process of setting something on fire in order to destroy it.|It is possible that περιάπτω, in view of the prefix περι-, adds a component of ‘round about,’ suggesting that the blaze or fire was for the benefit of those who encircled the fire.

senses.def: to set up or erect a construction, often used in connection with tents
any kind of boat, from small fishing boats as on Lake Galilee to large seagoing vessels
senses.comment: It may be very important to distinguish clearly between small fishing boats and larger ships or vessels. In a number of languages the distinction is based upon whether or not such vessels have decks. For the fishing boats on Lake Galilee there was probably no deck structure, while vessels going for long distances on the Mediterranean would certainly have had decks. See 6.42.

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
senses.def: from a point of time considerably prior to another point of time
senses.comment: It is also possible to interpret πόρρωθεν in Hebrews 11:13 as meaning ‘from afar’ or ‘from a great distance’ (see 83.31).

senses.def: a position at a relatively great distance, with the possible implication of comparison
senses.comment: In Hebrews 11:13 πόρρωθεν may be interpreted as time (see 67.46), but it is perhaps more satisfactorily interpreted as implying some visionary experience and hence a matter of space.

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of πρόδρομος ‘one who runs on ahead,’ not occurring in the NT) one who undergoes an experience in advance of others
senses.comment: In rendering πρόδρομος in Hebrews 6:20 it is important to avoid an expression which would suggest that Jesus simply ‘ran on ahead.’ The implication of πρόδρομος in this type of context is that of a precursor, that is to say, one who goes on ahead in order to show the way or to pioneer on behalf of someone else. Hebrews 6:20 may therefore be rendered as ‘Jesus went on ahead of us in there for our benefit.’

senses.def: the act of speaking to or making requests of God
senses.comment: In some languages there are a number of different terms used for prayer depending upon the nature of the content, for example, requests for material blessing, pleas for spiritual help, intercession for others, thanksgiving, and praise. There may also be important distinctions on the basis of urgency and need. The most generic expression for prayer may simply be ‘to speak to God.’ It is normally best to avoid an expression which means primarily ‘to recite.’

senses.def: (derivative of προσεύχομαι ‘to pray,’ 33.178) a place where people customarily meet to pray

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
senses.def: to do something at a point of time which immediately precedes another point of time
senses.comment: It would also be possible to render this expression in Matthew 17:25 as ‘Jesus spoke to Simon before Simon could speak to him.’

senses.def: to beat or strike repeatedly with a stick or rod
glosses: to beat with a stick or rod

senses.def: a person in the genealogy of Jesus
to pay special attention to something for the sake of a future recall and response
(derivative of σκοτία[a] ‘darkness,’ 14.53) to change from a condition of being light to one of being dark
senses.comment: In Revelation 9:2 it may not be difficult to speak of ‘the air becoming dark,’ since this would mean the space above the earth, but it may be difficult to speak of ‘the sun becoming dark.’ In the latter instance, for both Revelation 9:2 and Matthew 24:29, one may say ‘the sun will no longer shine’ or ‘the sun will not give its light.’|In place of ‘the air became dark,’ it is also possible to speak of ‘the sky will become dark.’

senses.def: (figurative extension of meaning of σκοτίζω[a] ‘to become dark,’ 14.55) to become unable to perceive and thus unable to understand
glosses: to not be able to understand
senses.comment: It is rare that one can combine the concept of ‘becoming dark’ with incapacity to understand or comprehend. Sometimes a parallel figure of speech may be employed by using an expression such as ‘to not be able to see.’ For example, in Romans 1:21 it is sometimes possible to translate ‘their foolish minds became unable to see the truth,’ and in Ephesians 4:18 it is sometimes possible to translate ‘they were not able to see with their minds.’

senses.def: the area on the top of a flat-roof house
senses.comment: In general, the types of roofs referred to in the NT are flat-top, made of pounded dirt, sometimes mixed with lime or stone, and supported by heavy beams. In view of the various types of activities described as taking place on the housetop, it may be important in some languages to indicate either in the text or in a marginal note the fact that such housetops were flat and that there was usually easy access to such roofs.

senses.def: to accompany in going down to
glosses: to go or come down together with

senses.def: (figurative extension of meaning employing the base πνίγω[a] ‘to choke,’ 19.53) to cause the death of plants by other plants crowding them out and/or overshadowing them
to crowd around to the point that one can hardly breathe (a very emphatic form)
to cause serious trouble to, with the implication of dire consequences and probably a weakened state
to join in attacking

senses.domain: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products
senses.def: the joint connecting the foot to the leg
one’s immediate offspring, but without specific reference to sex or age
senses.comment: In languages in which there is no generic term for ‘child’ or ‘offspring,’ one may use ‘son’ or ‘daughter’ or ‘son and daughter,’ singular or plural, depending upon the context.

senses.def: successive following generations of those who are biologically related to a reference person
senses.comment: In the case of γενεά[c], τέκνον[b], and σπέρμα[b] (10.29), the reference is not to one’s immediate descendants or offspring (that is to say, to one’s sons or daughters) but to a successive series of such persons, one’s descendants. In some languages such descendants may be called merely ‘the children of one’s children,’ and in other languages one may refer to descendants as ‘those who follow one’ or ‘those who come later.’

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of τέκνον[a] ‘child,’ 10.36) inhabitants of a particular place
senses.comment: Only rarely can one preserve the figurative significance of τέκνον[c] as a designation of the inhabitants of an area. Readers are too likely to understand such a reference as applicable only to children who live in a particular place. Even the use of a simile does not assist appreciably, since it would be interpreted as likening the inhabitants of an area to children, probably in the sense of their being immature or incapable. For example, the expression the people of Jerusalem like children would probably lead to serious misunderstanding.

senses.subdomain: Persons For Whom There Is Affectionate Concern
senses.def: (extension of meaning of τέκνον[a] ‘child, offspring,’ 10.36) a person of any age for whom there is a special relationship of endearment and association
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is impossible to translate τέκνον in Matthew 9:2 as ‘child,’ since this might immediately suggest that Jesus was declaring himself to be the father of this man. Furthermore, the paralytic was evidently an adult male. A more satisfactory equivalent would be ‘my dear man’ or ‘my dear fellow.’

senses.def: a person who looks to another as being, so to speak, a father in the faith and thus becomes a disciple of that person
senses.comment: It is also possible that τέκνον in 3 John 1:4 is to be understood simply as an affectionate way of talking about persons who in one way or another are in a dependent relationship to someone (see 9.46).

senses.def: a kind or class of persons, with the implication of possessing certain derived characteristics
glosses: one who has the characteristics of

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: children of light) persons to whom the truth of God has been revealed and who are presumably living according to such truth. See also 9.4 and 12.15
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is difficult to speak of ‘light’ in the metaphorical sense of the truth that comes from God. Such truth is not to be equated with knowledge, but with the principles and practices of right moral behavior. Because of these difficulties in speaking of ‘truth’ as ‘light,’ a number of translators have preferred to use the expression ‘people of God’ for the phrases υἱοὶ τοῦ φωτός, υἱοὶ τῆς ἡμέρας, and τέκνα φωτός. In some instances, however, it is possible to employ ‘light,’ if this is described as ‘light that comes from God’ or even ‘the true light from God.’

senses.def: pertaining to being of such a kind, often with the implication of a degree of uniqueness or distinctiveness

senses.domain: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products
senses.def: a visible impression or trace made as the result of a blow or pressure
senses.comment: Though both στίγμα[a] (8.55) and τύπος[a] may mean scars, there are significant differences in meaning. στίγμα[a] bears the connotation of brand or mark of ownership, while τύπος[a] indicates a wound or scar resulting from the shape and form of some object, for example, nails in the case of John 20:25.

senses.def: an object (not necessarily three-dimensional) which has been formed to resemble a person, god, animal, etc.
senses.comment: In certain contexts the referents of εἰκών[a], τύπος[b], and χάραγμα[b] may have special religious significance in that they may refer to idols, but the focal component for the translator is that of a likeness or resemblance. In contexts such as Matthew 22:20 an equivalent translation may be simply a picture, but in Romans 1:23 and Acts 7:43 one may use the same expression as is employed to render εἴδωλον[a] idol (6.97).

senses.subdomain: Pattern, Model, Example, and Corresponding Representation
senses.def: a visual form designed to be imitated or copied

senses.subdomain: Pattern, Model, Example, and Corresponding Representation
senses.def: a model of behavior as an example to be imitated or to be avoided
a model or example which anticipates or precedes a later realization
a kind or class, implying a relationship to some model or pattern
senses.comment: For another interpretation of τύπος in Acts 23:25, see 90.28.

senses.def: the content of a discourse or a document
senses.comment: For another interpretation of τύπος in Acts 23:25, see 58.25.

senses.def: pertaining to excessive boasting
senses.comment: In some languages the equivalent of ‘boastful words’ is ‘words too big for what one is talking about’ or ‘puffed up words’ or ‘swollen words.’

senses.def: (derivative of ὑφαίνω ‘to weave,’ 48.3) pertaining to being woven
senses.comment: In a number of languages it may be best to translate the last part of John 19:23 as simply ‘it was only one piece of cloth’ or ‘it was not made by sewing pieces of cloth together.’

senses.def: a false teacher in the church
to confine someone in prison
senses.comment: ‘To imprison a person’ is often expressed in somewhat idiomatic forms, for example, ‘to be tied inside’ or ‘to be locked in the dark’ or even ‘to eat one’s food with rats.’

senses.def: a woman whose husband has died
senses.comment: In rendering Mark 12:42 ‘poor widow’ may be translated as ‘poor woman whose husband had died.’

senses.def: one who claims to be an apostle but is not
